name: VARA
description: VARA estimates the sample variance (n-1) while treating text as 0 and logical values TRUE as 1 and FALSE as 0.
tldr: Sample variance that also counts text and logicals as numbers.

parameters.name: value1
parameters.description: The first value, range, or reference in the sample.

basicExample.description: Sample variance of numeric values only
basicExample.explanation: With only numbers present, VARA returns the same result as VAR.

advancedExamples.title: Text and TRUE are counted
advancedExamples.scenario: A range that mixes numbers, text, and a logical
advancedExamples.description: Text becomes 0 and TRUE becomes 1 before the calculation
advancedExamples.explanation: The values used are 10,20,30,1,0; the mean is 12.2 and the sample variance (sum of squared deviations 656.8 divided by 4) is 164.2.

advancedExamples.title: Contrast with VAR on a reference
advancedExamples.description: VAR ignores text and logicals inside a range
advancedExamples.explanation: VAR sees only 10,20,30 (n=3), variance 100, whereas VARA counts all five values for 164.2.

howItWorks: VARA first coerces every argument to a number (text to 0, TRUE to 1, FALSE to 0), then computes the sample variance with the n-1 denominator. Because non-numeric entries count toward both the sum and the mean, they change the variance materially.

howToSteps.name: Identify values
howToSteps.text: Collect the values, including any text or logicals you want counted.

howToSteps.name: Press Enter
howToSteps.text: The sample variance including non-numerics is shown.

limitations: Counting text as 0 can distort the result when text cells are labels, not true zeros.
Still requires at least two effective values, otherwise returns #DIV/0!.
The n-1 denominator still assumes a sample, not a full population (use VARPA for population).

commonErrors.cause: Fewer than two effective numeric values after coercion.
commonErrors.fix: Provide at least two values that evaluate to numbers.

commonErrors.cause: Text labels were coerced to 0, pulling the mean down.
commonErrors.fix: Use VAR when text cells should be ignored.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: VARA is available in Google Sheets with the same coercion rules.

faq.question: Does VARA treat empty cells as 0?
faq.answer: No. Empty cells are ignored; only text and logicals are coerced (text to 0, TRUE to 1, FALSE to 0).

faq.question: When should I use VARA instead of VAR?
faq.answer: When your data includes logicals or text that genuinely represent 1/0 or zero, and you want them in the sample.

faq.question: What is the population equivalent?
faq.answer: VARPA, which uses the n denominator instead of n-1.
